payload.recallText: I was a freshman at Fordham in the Bronx, just at the time when they decided that they were going to go against their mission of serving middle and lower class kids. They jacked up the tuition to bring in all the rich kids. One day, I saw the person who was responsible for this change, Dean McGowan on the steps of the school. I said to him, Dean, is it true that you're not going to stick up for the poors? He replied Fuck you. Out of the corner of my eye, I saw this guy come out of the wings and throw a pie in Dean McGowan's face. I called him Pie Man, capital P, capital M because what he did was really good. I then went back to the Fordham newspaper and told the editor about my story. He said I could go with it. The editor was a tall guy who would go on to win a Pulitzer. I wrote the story and it ran. I actually wrote five stories about this issue, and all five of them ran. I saw the Dean again and the Pie Man appeared and threw another pie at the Dean's face. He said, "Ego sum non bestia", I am not a beast and he ran away again. Then I saw Sheila, head of the Student Body. She was drinking at the bar. I had been flirting with her for two months, but it was one of those things where she didn't even know I was flirting with her. So I turned around and guess who was tapping me on the shoulder? It was Sheila. She asked me if I was Pie Man. I wanted to say that I had never seen his face, but I didn't. I said, "Sure, I'm Pie Man. What do you want to know?"
